items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: this fellow, Mr. Satterwhite, that owned the place, would hire two musicians

ctx.x: But anyway, I accepted this and gladly took it, because it really was my pleasure. So I started on this job. We worked seven days a week, and my salary was twelve dollars a week. I was just happy I was making... I felt like I was making good money and working!

During this time, what I learned was that this fellow, Mr. Satterwhite, that owned the place, would hire two musicians, and before the night was over, we would have anywhere from 8 to 10, and sometimes even 12 musicians up there playing, and it would be guys that would drop in from other places or other jobs that they had. At that time, Washington had five big bands, big local bands in it, and there were... One band, Bill Baldwin's Syncopators played at a place on the 1200 block of U Street called the Lincoln…

Just two blocks down the street from there, at Tenth and U Street, was the Masonic Ballroom, where they featured two bands. One was called... A fellow named Pete Moss had a band, and there was another fellow who I think is still around, and his name was Bill Hester, and Bill Hester called his band The Bluebirds.
